title: Weight Bridge: curation, conversion, deterministic smoke-validation, and canonical pin publish
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal:
Build an end-to-end "weight-bridge" orchestrator that reliably takes community weights (HF/Git LFS manifests), converts to our runtime artifacts, runs deterministic smoke-validation across target variants, and publishes a canonical pin + performance profile to the model catalog.

Scope and non-goals:
- Include ingestion (signed manifests, provenance extraction), format conversion (safe quantize/convert paths), deterministic smoke suites, lightweight perf profiling, canonical pin heuristics and publish flows.
- Not in scope: long-running heavy benchmarking (that remains on the perf pipeline), or cost-optimization autotuning (handled by Optimize later).

Key decisions made so far:
- Use content-hash + manifest signature for canonical pins; pins map to a primary artifact + variant family rather than a single binary to allow automated fallback. (Reason: preserves reproducibility while enabling runtime flexibility.)
- Deterministic smoke-validation will include: token-level generation for a fixed prompt set, KV-cache snapshot equivalence checks, and a minimal latency/memory profile at 128/1024 context lengths. We accepted reduced coverage in exchange for fast pre-publish feedback (~30–45s per variant).
- Conversion steps will attempt a lossless pathway first; when quantization is required we produce both int8 and int4 quantized variants and tag them clearly. We will mark quantized variants with a "quality delta" score to surface potential regressions.

Trade-offs & rationale:
- Strict vs permissive gates: We chose a two-tier gate. Automatic publish if all deterministic checks pass AND signature/provenance verified; otherwise route to a manual review queue with pre-attached artifacts. This balances automation velocity with safety for high-risk artifacts.
- Compute vs latency for validation: To keep onboarding throughput acceptable, we run smoke-validation on a small fleet of preemptible GPUs and cap end-to-end work to 2 minutes per model family for automated flow. Models that exceed this are flagged for extended profiling.

Work completed:
- Prototype converter service (repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/weight-bridge) with initial PR #412 implementing HF-to-runtime conversion.
- Manifest signer/validator implemented; initial attestations validated against https://secrets.redwood.ai/kms.
- Sample deterministic prompt-suite authored (drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1KWeightSuiteExample) and integrated into smoke runner.

Open implementation tasks / TODOs:
- Integrate the converter with the ingestion queue and add retry semantics (backoff + dead-letter).
- Implement canonical pin conflict resolution algorithm (currently a simple latest-stable heuristic; needs bump rules).
- Build UI hooks for Console: publish preview page, variant diff, and revert flow. Frontend spec in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/weight-bridge-runbook
- End-to-end e2e tests that operate on ephemeral infra + signed manifests (automation story in CI).

Blockers:
- Pending KMS key access for the staging weight-bridge service (security team approval queued: SEC-457).
- Autoscaler quotas in the staging cluster — request with infra team (ticket INFRA-2211).

Observability & rollout plan:
- Telemetry: publish onboarding traces to Console with per-step timings, conversion error classes, and smoke-diff metrics. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/models/onboard/ENG-684210 (WIP).
- Rollout: start as opt-in automation for community model submissions, route high-risk models to explicit manual review. Canary on small subset of community weights for two weeks then expand.

Acceptance criteria:
- Given a signed HF manifest, the pipeline ingests, converts into runtime artifacts, runs deterministic smoke-suite, and either: publishes canonical pin + profile OR creates a manual-review entry with diagnostics.
- Canonical pin publish creates a stable pin record with: content-hash, variant-family mapping, a minimal perf profile (latency p50/p95 at 128/1024), and a provenance URI.

Notes for reviewers:
- Review focus: pin conflict resolution heuristics, acceptable failure modes to trigger manual review, and security assumptions around signed manifests and KMS.

Next steps:
- Finish autoscale/quotas unblock (INFRA-2211), complete KMS security sign-off (SEC-457), wireup publish flows with Console previews, and run 50-canary ingest jobs across diverse OSS weights to validate throughput and signal quality before full launch.
